text:
incident-bot: ALERT: cb-runtime-euwest1 experiencing sustained tail latency > 3x baseline and memory growth on kv-cache shard pool. Error spike observed for request type=chat.generate across multiple backends. INC-ID: INC-2026-342 :rotating_light:

maya (oncall): on it. grabbing traces + current deploy hash. maya (oncall): root cause hypothesis?

arjun: early signal looks like continuous-batching window jitter + aggressive prefetch heuristic causing KV cache blowup under high concurrency. eviction rate spiked, OOM-ish behavior caused throttling and queued requests.

samir: corroborating — telemetry shows microbatch_size distribution shifted up (median microbatch tokens ~3x normal) after 2am rollout of prefetch-v2. kv_cache_entries increased linearly for ~12s bursts then eviction churn.

olivia: rolling back prefetch-v2 now would be fastest. deploying revert build to canary first. request control-plane to pause any autopromote.

incident-bot: Pager: @maya (oncall) @arjun @olivia @samir — severity P1. Channel #incidents created: #inc-2026-342.

maya (oncall): plan: 1) stop prefetch heuristic on runtime nodes 2) reduce batch_window_ms to reduce microbatch growth 3) enable KV throttling (per-shard max_inflight_requests) 4) communicate customer impact to Support. Who can flip the runtime flag?

olivia: I can push the flag. command I'm going to run on canaries:```sh
redwoodctl runtime set-config --cluster cb-runtime-euwest1 --key runtime.prefetch.enabled --value false --target canary
```

olivia: then promote to 20% then 100% if canaries are stable. expected change: reduce median microbatch size quickly.

jordan: Also recommend lowering runtime.batch_window_ms from 40 -> 12 for the next 10m. That limits batch accumulation under jitter. I can apply:```json
{"runtime.batch_window_ms": 12, "runtime.max_inflight_per_shard": 64}
```

samir: quick note: lowering batch_window_ms will increase CPU overhead per token slightly but should collapse kv cache growth. eviction spikes might persist for a short period until caches settle.

arjun: also set kv_cache.max_entries_per_shard=100000 temporarily to cap growth and throttle prefetches.

olivia: applying canary changes now (start 1769056895)

deploy-bot: deploy started: revert-prefetch-canary @olivia (deploy id: dply-2026-889).

olivia: canary logs show median microbatch tokens dropping from ~120 to ~24 within 30s. eviction rate down ~70%.

maya (oncall): good. rolling to 20% (1769057012). monitor for 2m.

kevin: customer-impact: Support reports 4 customer tenants (acme-inc, finserv-co, edu-labs, searchly) with elevated 5xx rates ~8-12% and tail latency 3–7s for chat endpoints starting 02:04 UTC. No data exfiltration.

support: opened high-touch escalations for acme-inc + finserv-co. CS is sending status update template, ETA for stabilization 10–15m.

olivia: promoted to 100% at 1769057128. all runtime nodes now have prefetch disabled and batch_window_ms=12.

incident-bot: automation check: memory usage trending down across shards; 95th p99 latency trending toward baseline.

maya (oncall): mitigation effective. next step: patch the prefetch heuristic to respect per-shard token budget and fallback on heavy concurrency. We'll schedule a rollback-release pipeline for prefetch-v2 with new guardrails.

arjun: docs for hotfix we'll ship: change prefetch window scaling to clamp by runtime.max_batch_tokens and add exponential backoff after eviction event. Also add metric: prefetch_tokens_queued.

samir: we should add an emergency runbook item: when kv_cache_entries_rate > X and eviction_rate > Y, auto-throttle prefetch at cluster level (kill prefetch tokeners for 30s).

maya (oncall): customer impact summary for postmortem: - incident start 1769056789 (02:03:09 UTC) - root trigger: prefetch-v2 rollout changes batch formation under high concurrency -> microbatch blowup -> kv cache growth -> eviction churn -> increased tail latency and 5xxs. - Affected: 4 named tenants, ~10% error rate peak, brief customer-visible errors for ~12min. - Mitigation: disabled prefetch + reduced batch_window_ms + kv cap, rolled canary -> full release; stabilization at 1769057320 (02:16:00 UTC).

maya (oncall): handing off to arjun for follow-up and postmortem. I'm marking incident resolved in 20m unless we see recurrence.

arjun: I'll own the follow-up. immediate actions: 1) add guardrail to prefetch, 2) add autoscaler rule to detect kv blowout and auto-throttle, 3) postmortem draft in #postmortems with timeline + customer comms.

support: sent customer updates to impacted tenants and offered them SLO credits for the window.

jordan: monitoring TODOs: add alert for sustained increase in microbatch median tokens + correlated kv_cache_entries growth. also add a dashboard tile for per-shard eviction_rate.

maya (oncall): thanks team. please add any relevant logs/config snippets to the incident doc. I'll de-escalate paging for now. :white_check_mark: 

olivia: pasting useful snippet of canary check command:```sh
redwoodctl runtime get-metrics --cluster cb-runtime-euwest1 --metric microbatch.token_count --window 60s --agg median,p95
```

samir: one-more-note: prefetch-v2 had optimistic batching when sample load < 200ms; that heuristic fails under bursty high concurrency. We'll change to conservative initial window and ramp up.

incident-bot: Incident INC-2026-342 marked as mitigated by maya (oncall) at 1769057320. Postmortem owner: arjun.

maya (oncall): closing handoff. I'll follow up in postmortem with timeline + whether we should throttle new prefetch rollouts behind a feature gate.

arjun: will file PRs for guardrail changes and include regression tests that simulate high concurrency jitter.

kevin: logging the customer SLO notes and support ticket IDs in the incident doc (TKT-8791, TKT-8792).

maya (oncall): thanks all. end thread.
